claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy-alloy derivatives have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
Annealing at 500°C for 2 hours will increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy-alloy derivatives.
Annealing at 500°C for 2 hours relaxes internal stresses in these alloys.
Annealing at 500°C for 2 hours reduces lattice-defect density in these alloys.
Internal-stress relaxation and lattice-defect reduction introduce magnetic anisotropy.
The introduced magnetic anisotropy increases coercivity.
The annealed material will have a coercive field at least 20% greater than that of the as-cast or as-prepared material.
An inert or vacuum annealing atmosphere prevents oxidation.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on alloy composition and initial microstructure.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires an increase of at least 20%, but the hypothesis is falsified only when the increase is below 10%. An increase from 10% to less than 20% would fail the stated prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
